title: Jacob Wrestles Before Meeting Esau
overview: Jacob heads home to face the brother he cheated twenty years earlier, and the night before they meet he wrestles a mysterious stranger and is given a new name.

parts.label: God's camp at Mahanaim (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: As Jacob nears home, angels meet him, and he names the place Mahanaim, which means "two camps." The name seems to set up the chapter: God's camp beside Jacob's, and soon Jacob splitting his own people into two camps.

parts.label: A humble message, an alarming reply (vv. 3-8)
parts.note: Years before, Jacob tricked Esau out of the firstborn's rights and their father's blessing, and Esau vowed to kill him, so now Jacob calls Esau "my lord" and himself "your servant." The text does not say why Esau brings 400 men, but Jacob fears the worst and divides everyone so that at least half might escape.

parts.label: Jacob's prayer (vv. 9-12)
parts.note: Jacob reminds God of the promise to bring him home safely and admits he deserves none of the kindness he has received. He left with only a walking stick and now returns as "two camps," yet he is openly terrified for his wives and children.

parts.label: Gifts sent in waves (vv. 13-21)
parts.note: Jacob sends more than 550 animals, a huge fortune, in separate herds, each servant repeating the same message that Jacob is coming behind. The text says he hoped these gifts would calm Esau before they met face to face.

parts.label: Wrestling at the Jabbok (vv. 22-29)
parts.note: Alone at night by the Jabbok stream, Jacob wrestles a man who turns out to be more than a man; the text links him with God, and the later prophet Hosea calls him an angel. Jacob, whose name sounds like "heel" and came to suggest a grabber or cheat, refuses to let go and is renamed Israel, which the text explains as "struggles with God."

parts.label: Peniel and the limp (vv. 30-32)
parts.note: Jacob names the place Peniel, "face of God," amazed that he saw God and lived, but he walks away limping. The story explains a Jewish custom still kept today of not eating a tendon in an animal's hip, traditionally identified as the sciatic nerve.

disagreement: Christians differ over who the wrestler was (an angel, God appearing in human form, or, as some Christians read it, Christ before his birth) and whether the struggle was a physical event or a vision.
think: What do you think makes it so hard to face someone we have wronged, and what does it take to finally do it?
